A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaT framework and PCS filtering method. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original personalization experiments, sample-diversity and filtering ablations, and a human evaluation in Figure 8.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds multi-concept results in Table 2 and observation/filtering experiments in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: v3 adds merging concept trees into scenario-specific forests and applying cross-tree attribute constraints for multi-concept synthesis (Sections 3.2 and 4.2; Figure 4b). This is a limited procedural extension: the original tree construction, three editing operations, and PCS filtering remain.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates single-concept personalization, explicitly using the single-concept portion of MC-LLaVA. v3 adds multi-concept evaluation in Table 2, substantially extending the task to handling multiple concepts within shared scenes. The original three benchmark sources remain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 5 adds DINOv2, combined encoders, and GPT-4o as filtering comparisons against CLIP. The personalization comparators in Table 1 and the earlier no-filter, cosine-similarity, and PCS comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments apply controlled sample-composition comparisons to MC-LLaVA and MyVLM model configurations and test alternative filtering encoders/VLMs (Appendices B–C). The original reported splits, reference-image counts, LLaVA-1.5-13B backbone, and PCS thresholds remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns of the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted checks of sample-role observations across datasets and models (Figures 3 and 7), negative-sample PCS/diversity measurements (Table 4), and filtering-encoder dependence (Table 5). Existing tree-editing, data-component, filtering, hard-negative generation, and human analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The additional PCS distributions and result tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial multi-concept results and new observation/filtering results. Table 1 also revises the MC-LLaVA real-data baseline on MC-LLaVA: recognition changes from 0.912 to 0.917, VQA BLEU from 0.679 to 0.684, and caption recall from 0.741 to 0.750. Corresponding augmented-method scores remain unchanged, reducing reported margins rather than demonstrating improved method performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical tree representation, dataset construction, editing operations, feature extraction, and cosine-similarity equations remain equivalent. The forest extension is described procedurally without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The core claims about controllable synthetic data, PCS filtering, and personalization from 1–3 reference images remain. The abstract and introduction newly advertise multi-concept support through forests, which v1 treated as a future extension.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations about preventing cross-concept attribute overlap and the performance–cost tradeoff of stronger filtering models. Table 1 narrows its GPT-4o comparability statement from all methods to MC-LLaVA, and the RAP-MLLM limitation discussion is removed. Appendix H nevertheless retains the assertion that multiple concepts cannot be handled, contradicting the new applicability claims.

D1.justification: v1's released-code statement and CaT repository link become 'The code will be released' in v3. v3 also omits the documented rules disabling Add at five or more dimensions, disabling Remove at three or fewer, and otherwise balancing operations. This establishes lost documentation, not that those rules actually stopped being used. Most model settings and prompt templates remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including UnicTokens, LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave, and a synthetic-data survey, while removing User-VLM 360 and several general VLM references. The central positioning as a controllable synthesis framework complementing existing personalization methods remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes supporting material: data-quality related work and hard-negative/data-component analyses move from the main text into an A–H appendix structure, with the existing filtering study regrouped under ablations. The title, author list, introductory prose, PCS explanation, and numerous captions are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from three to six panels, Figure 4 adds a forest panel, and Figure 6 replaces four PCS pie charts with density curves. v3 adds three tables and an observation figure, restyles Table 1, and relocates existing displays. The extensive appendix concept-tree examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional multi-concept evaluation and model/filtering checks strengthen empirical coverage, and revised Table 1 comparisons improve numerical reporting. However, the central new multi-concept capability contradicts the retained Appendix H limitation, while code-access information and implementation rules are removed. These unresolved clarity and reproducibility losses prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
